questions.q: What does "shift left" mean, per this lesson?
options: Moving the point where a problem gets caught earlier in the development timeline, away from production
Moving database servers to a different data center region
Switching from T-SQL to a left-associative query language
Reducing the number of columns in a table
questions.explain: The name is literal — moving detection toward the left edge of a dev-to-production timeline, ideally into code or code review.

questions.q: Without shift-left practices, where does this lesson say a bad migration typically surfaces?
options: In production, discovered through a slow page and an alert that pages an on-call DBA
It never surfaces at all
Only during the developer's annual performance review
In the database vendor's changelog
questions.explain: Without earlier checks, the same problem tends to surface as a live incident rather than a code-review comment.

questions.q: In the lesson's CI example, what happens to a migration before it can merge?
options: It runs against a throwaway copy of the schema, and is checked for destructive changes and missing indexes
It is emailed to the DBA for a manual signature
It is automatically deployed straight to production for testing
Nothing — CI only runs after a change has already deployed
questions.explain: The example CI stage validates the migration against a scratch schema copy and runs automated checks before merge.

questions.q: What is this lesson's core argument for why shift-left is worth doing?
options: Cost — a problem caught in review is far cheaper to fix than the same problem caught in production
It is required by SQL Server licensing terms
It eliminates the need for any testing in production ever
It is purely a matter of team morale with no cost benefit
questions.explain: The lesson frames the case for shift-left as cost, not virtue: a comment and a quick fix versus an incident and a postmortem.

questions.q: How does this lesson connect shift-left database practices to earlier material in the course?
options: It ties shift-left directly to the CI/CD pipeline built in Chapter 4
It has no connection to any earlier chapter
It replaces everything taught about IaC in Chapter 5
It argues Chapter 4's CI/CD pipeline should be removed
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly frames the CI/CD pipeline from Chapter 4 as where shift-left database practices actually run.
